text:
devon: Heads-up — after last night's runtime deploy we saw ~15-25% tail latency regressions on paged-attn workloads. Flamegraph and traces here: https://internal.perf/fg/1767004321 (internal). Initial triage points to hot allocation spikes in kv_pager_alloc() and increased block-table churn. Repro steps: run paged-attn mixed-batch (seqs up to 8192) with bursty traffic. pprof snippet below.

maria: Yep repro'd on my local canary. Noticeable when seq_len > 4096 and batch_size >= 8. Allocation churn starts ~2s into the request.

sasha: I ran a microtrace — block-table growth correlates with kernel selector switching to FA-variant-3 for long sequences. FA-3 seems to touch memory earlier (prefault style) which looks like it trips pager paths.

runtime-bot: Deploy note: rollout 2026-03-16T02:12 triggered canary on cluster dedicated-eu (build sha: db1a3f).

nora: Can you paste the heap diff / pprof top? Any recent pager config changes? I think we bumped kv_page_size 64 -> 128 in the last patch.

devon: pprof heap delta (allocated objects):
```
1.  312K  34.2%  34.2%  kv_page_entry (object)
2.  188K  20.6%  54.8%  block_table_node
3.  102K  11.2%  66.0%  kv_slot_meta
```
Also saw frequent allocations at kv_pager_alloc -> block_table_grow -> slab_alloc.

ben: Quick hypothesis: FA-3's memory access pattern forces earlier page population which increases live KV page set; combined with current slab policy (per-request alloc/free) we get fragmentation and GC churn. Two fixes: A) prefer non-prefaulting kernels for paged workloads or B) move to pooled/slab allocator for block tables so we don't constantly allocate/free.

maria: Also our batching heuristic recently changed to favor larger effective windows for throughput — that increases per-request KV footprint. Suggest adding a soft cap on "active_kv_pages" per session and LRU eviction when cap exceeded. Keeps p95 in check.

sasha: Microbenchmark results I ran (mixed batches, 50% long):
- FA-2: throughput 100 req/s, p95 120ms, allocs/sec 18
- FA-3: throughput 112 req/s, p95 146ms, allocs/sec 36
So FA-3 gives throughput but doubles alloc churn and worsens tail.

devon: Proposed immediate action: rollback kernel selector change so FA-3 is opt-in for paged-attn; land allocator change to pre-allocate block_table slabs (power-of-two slab sizes) to reduce fragmentation; add soft cap to batching config. Can we canary these quickly?

nora: Agree. I'll schedule a canary with selector rollback + allocator patch toggles. @runtime-bot start canary when PRs land.

runtime-bot: Canary request queued: will start on PR merge.

ben: I'll open a small RFC describing the pooled allocator and add perf tests for sequence-length distributions (will include alloc-rate metrics in CI).

devon: TL;DR/root cause: interplay between kernel memory-touch pattern (FA-3), batching heuristics increasing live KV window, and a per-request allocator that fragments block tables. Action items: rollback selector, canary allocator + cap, RFC + perf tests, incident ticket. Thanks everyone. (reacts :eyes:)
